chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bought a slave girl and had intercourse with her, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he finds a defect in her, it is not for him to return her, but he is returned the value of what the defect diminished [her price].' I said, 'Is this the saying of Ali (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man finds a defect in a slave girl after having intercourse with her?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific application of *khiyar al-'ib* (option of defect) in the context of purchasing a slave girl, distinguishing it from general sales by ruling that consummation prevents full return but entitles the buyer to proportional compensation for the defect's impact on value. The Imam’s confirmation that this aligns with the practice of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) underscores the continuity of Imami jurisprudence with the foundational authority of the Ahl al-Bayt. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise valuation (*qimah*) over simple restitution in cases where the item has been utilized.
